Research Letters"],"published-print":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,16]]},"abstract":"<jats:title>Abstract<\/jats:title>\n                  <jats:p>We conducted a 220\u2010m mesh simulation over the global domain with realistic topography. This can be called a first \u201cglobal large\u2010eddy simulation\u201d (GLES) for deep convection. The resolution dependence across km\u2010 to sub\u2010km scales and sensitivity to turbulence schemes are investigated. The results showed that the too\u2010intense localized precipitation frequently produced in km\u2010scale models, known as \u201cpopcorn\u2010like\u201d precipitation, weakens as resolution increases. Although zonal mean precipitation differs substantially across turbulence schemes at km\u2010scale resolution, it decreases as resolution increases, indicating convergence across the schemes. Low cloud fraction decreases with increasing resolution, whereas the resolution dependence of high cloud fraction depends on the turbulence scheme: it increases for the Smagorinsky\u2010type scheme and decreases for the Mellor\u2010Yamada\u2010type schemes. The response of low cloud distribution differs between the turbulence schemes. The present results indicate that GLES is promising for simulating precipitation intensity, while cloud simulation remains
